sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The historical period and reign of **Emperor Harshavardhana** (also known as **Harsha**), the last prominent Hindu emperor of ancient India.
Ruled from **606 AD to 647 AD** during the **7th Century CE**.
Northern and Northwestern India, initially from **Thanesar** (Haryana) and later shifting his capital to **Kannauj** (Uttar Pradesh).
Founder of the dynasty was **Pushyabhuti**; prominent rulers included **Prabhakarvardhana**, **Rajyavardhana**, and **Harshavardhana**.
Marked the transition of ancient India into the early medieval period; made **Kannauj** the political center of Northern India.
Patron of arts and literature, author of three Sanskrit plays (**Ratnavali**, **Priyadarsika**, **Nagananda**), and patronized **Nalanda University**.
Crucial Uttar Pradesh-specific historical topic due to **Kannauj** and **Prayag (Allahabad)** assemblies.
The famous Chinese Buddhist traveler **Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang)** visited India and stayed in Harsha's court during his reign.
Initially a worshipper of **Shiva (Maheshwara)**, later deeply influenced by Mahayana Buddhism through **Hiuen Tsang**.

items.title: 1. Rise of the Pushyabhuti Dynasty
items.content:
• **Origin:** Rose to prominence after the decline of the **Gupta Empire** and the Hun invasions.
• **Founder:** **Pushyabhuti** was the original founder, but **Prabhakarvardhana** was the first powerful independent ruler.
• **Titles:** Prabhakarvardhana assumed titles like **Maharajadhiraja** and **Paramabhattaraka**.
• **Family:** Married his daughter **Rajyashri** to **Grahavarman** of the **Maukhari dynasty** of Kannauj.
• **Mnemonic for Family Members:** **'P-R-R-H'** -> **P**rabhakarvardhana (Father) -> **R**ajyavardhana (Brother) -> **R**ajyashri (Sister) -> **H**arshavardhana (Self).

items.title: 2. Ascension and Consolidation of Harsha
items.content:
• **Accession Year:** Crowned king at the young age of **16 years** in **606 AD**.
• **Tragedy:** Elder brother **Rajyavardhana** was treacherously killed by **Shashanka** (King of Gauda/Bengal) and **Devagupta** (Malwa).
• **Vow:** Harsha took a vow to avenge his brother and rescue his widowed sister **Rajyashri** from the Vindhya forests.
• **Capital Shift:** Shifted his capital from **Thanesar** to **Kannauj** to strategically manage Northern Indian politics.
• **Military Expansion:** United large parts of Northern India under his direct control within six years.

items.title: 3. Conflict with Pulakeshin II
items.content:
• **Ambition:** Harsha wanted to expand his empire south of the **Narmada River**.
• **Opponent:** Met stiff resistance from the powerful Chalukya king **Pulakeshin II**.
• **Battle Details:** Fought on the banks of the **Narmada River** around **630-634 AD**.
• **Result:** **Pulakeshin II** decisively defeated **Harshavardhana**, halting his southward expansion.
• **Source:** Detailed description available in the **Aihole Inscription** composed by **Ravikirti**.

items.title: 4. Literary Patronage and Court Scholars
items.content:
• **Banabhatta:** Celebrated court poet who wrote **Harshacharita** (biography of Harsha) and **Kadambari**.
• **Harsha's Works:** Himself a renowned scholar, wrote three Sanskrit dramas: **Ratnavali**, **Priyadarsika**, and **Nagananda**.
• **Other Scholars:** **Matanga Divakara** and the Buddhist philosopher **Bhartrihari** adorned his court.
• **Financial Support:** Donated one-fourth of state revenue for the patronage of scholars, artists, and religious institutions.

items.title: 5. Hiuen Tsang and the Religious Assemblies
items.content:
• **Hiuen Tsang:** Visited India between **629 AD and 645 AD**, studying at **Nalanda University** under **Shilabhadra**.
• **Si-Yu-Ki:** Written records by Hiuen Tsang provide invaluable socio-economic and religious data on Harsha's administration.
• **Kannauj Assembly (643 AD):** Organized to honor Hiuen Tsang and propagate Mahayana Buddhism; attended by **20 kings** and thousands of monks.
• **Prayag Assembly (Mahamoksha Parishad):** Held every **5 years** at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna; Harsha distributed all accumulated royal wealth in charity.

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Ruled Thanesar and Kannauj; united Northern India temporarily.
First independent ruler, expanded territory against Huns.
Short reign; killed by Shashanka of Gauda while avenging sister's honor.
Greatest ruler of the dynasty; patron of arts, literature, and Buddhism.
Chalukya king of Badami; defeated Harsha on the banks of the Narmada.
Court poet of Harsha; wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari.
Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler; wrote 'Si-Yu-Ki'.
Head abbot and Chancellor of Nalanda University during Hiuen Tsang's visit.

items.definition: Acronym: **'PRN'** -> **P**riyadarsika, **R**atnavali, **N**agananda. Remember that Harsha wrote **P-R-N** plays in Sanskrit.
Acronym: **'BHABHI'** -> **Bha**nabhatta (Author), **Hi**uen Tsang (Visitor), **Bha**rtrihari (Scholar). Helps recall major figures in Harsha's empire.
Sequence: **Thanesar -> Kannauj**. Think of **'T.K.'** (Thanesar to Kannauj) as the political shift that made UP the center of power.
Rule of 5: The **Mahamoksha Parishad** at Prayag was held every **5 years**, where Harsha gave away all his gold and royal garments.
Association: **Harsha vs Pulakeshin II** on the **Narmada River** (Southern boundary check). Harsha lost, Pulakeshin won.
Students often think **Harshavardhana** founded the Pushyabhuti dynasty. **Correction:** **Pushyabhuti** was the actual founder; Harsha was the most famous ruler.
Confusing Chinese travelers. **Correction:** **Fa-Hien** came during Chandragupta II (Gupta period), whereas **Hiuen Tsang** came during **Harshavardhana**'s reign.
Assuming Harsha conquered all of India. **Correction:** Harsha was **defeated** by **Pulakeshin II** in the south, restricting his empire to Northern India.
Mixing up who wrote what. **Correction:** **Banabhatta** wrote *Harshacharita* (biography of Harsha), but **Harsha himself** wrote *Ratnavali*, *Priyadarsika*, and *Nagananda*.
Believing Harsha was a Buddhist from birth. **Correction:** He started as a devout worshipper of **Shiva (Maheshwara)** and converted/inclined towards Buddhism later.
Also known as the **Pushyabhuti dynasty** or the **Vardhana dynasty**, ruling from Thanesar and Kannauj.
Harshavardhana ascended the throne in **606 AD** at the age of 16 after his brother's assassination.
Shifted from **Thanesar** (Haryana) to **Kannauj** (Uttar Pradesh), making Kannauj the imperial capital of North India.
Assumed the title of **Siladitya** and was referred to as the lord of the north (**Sakalottarapathanath**).
Stopped at the **Narmada River** by Chalukya king **Pulakeshin II** in **634 AD**.
**Hiuen Tsang** (Xuanzang), the Prince of Pilgrims, visited India and praised Harsha's administration and law enforcement.
**Nalanda University** flourished under Harsha's royal patronage, receiving revenue from **200 villages**.
Harsha authored three Sanskrit plays: **Ratnavali**, **Priyadarsika**, and **Nagananda**.
**Banabhatta** wrote **Harshacharita** in Sanskrit prose, documenting the early life and conquests of Harsha.
Organized the **Kannauj Assembly** (643 AD) and the **Prayag Assembly** (Mahamoksha Parishad) for religious discussions and charity.
Harshavardhana died in **647 AD** without any direct heirs, leading to political fragmentation in Northern India.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on Uttar Pradesh-centric locations like **Kannauj** and **Prayag**, as well as authors and their texts (e.g., Banabhatta and Hiuen Tsang).
Remember the exact dates of Hiuen Tsang's visit (**629–645 AD**) and Harsha's reign (**606–647 AD**) as chronological questions are common.
UPSSSC frequently asks who defeated Harsha. Do not confuse the victor: it was **Pulakeshin II** (Chalukya dynasty), not the Pallavas or Guptas.
Watch out for trick questions distinguishing between books written BY Harsha versus books written ABOUT Harsha.

keyTakeaways: Harshavardhana ruled from **606 to 647 AD** and shifted his capital from **Thanesar** to **Kannauj**.
The Chinese traveler **Hiuen Tsang** visited India during Harsha's reign and studied at **Nalanda University**.
Harsha was defeated by Chalukya ruler **Pulakeshin II** on the banks of the **Narmada River**.
Harsha himself composed three Sanskrit plays: **Ratnavali**, **Priyadarsika**, and **Nagananda**.
He organized the **Kannauj Assembly** and the **Prayag Mahamoksha Parishad** for religious harmony and massive charity.
